The test image shows a banana leaf with:
- Large area of yellow-brown discoloration covering most of the leaf center
- Dark brown/black spots scattered throughout the yellowed zone
- Green healthy tissue remaining at the edges
- Mottled, blotchy pattern rather than discrete spots

This pattern of extensive yellowing with dark necrotic speckling is characteristic of Sigatoka diseases. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka image shows discrete oval lesions with dark centers and yellow halos on green leaf. The test image shows a more diffuse, confluent large yellow-brown area with dark mottled speckling throughout — potentially an advanced/coalesced stage.

Comparing:
- Test: large confluent yellow-tan zone with dark brown speckling, green tissue on margins
- Sigatoka reference: discrete spots with yellow halos — somewhat different but consistent with advanced coalescence
- Cigar_End_Rot/Bunchy_Top don't affect leaf tissue this way
- Panama Disease causes more uniform yellowing from margins

The mottled yellow-brown with dark necrotic spots across the leaf is most consistent with Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka at an advanced stage where individual lesions have merged.
